## Zero-volume tetrahedra in the Gmsh-generated in-memory mesh

A controlled same-XAO, same-installed-backend reproduction produced an exported
mesh byte-identical to the historical exported file. Pre-export inspection
found the same exactly coplanar, zero-volume tetrahedra already present in the
Gmsh-generated in-memory mesh, and reloading the ASCII mesh retained their
element and connectivity identities. ASCII serialization was therefore not
their origin in this reproduction. Element counts, coordinates, attributes,
consumers, and private run data are intentionally omitted.

The inspected public software identities were SCGSim `1.0.0.dev18` at
`a8ff06f5f568ac2bdfdc4f6a1c686cac59b9ab5d`, Palace source
`1ea14a84f60f672ffe4ce12dad404bc82896ef11`, and Palace binary SHA-256
`114157cd73ad45f74927d7840f8b72d8b0a306da7a60e3e93abf5e2c5f0c05e5`.
Gmsh was version `4.15.2`. These identities are provenance, not eligibility
criteria.

### What was and was not established

At that SCGSim revision, `_validate_tetrahedral_solution_groups` in
`src/scgsim/palace/_mesh.py` verifies solution-volume ownership, tetrahedral
element type, and the presence of 3D elements. It does not check signed
tetrahedron volume or element Jacobians. Native orientation handling accounts
for negative orientation; it does not make a zero determinant valid. Palace
`--dry-run` checks configuration and referenced-file availability, not the
quality of the constructed runtime mesh.

Later observations included extreme processed-mesh $\kappa$ and $h$ metrics,
the literal symptom `PCG solver did NOT converge` at 1000 iterations, later
GMRES failure or slow Arnoldi progress, and anomalous surface energy or
participation. These are associated symptoms, not proof of one common cause. In
particular, that PCG solve is the divergence-free projection, not the AMR
estimator or proof that a preconditioner is broken. `eig.csv` `Error (Abs.)` is
an algebraic eigenpair residual, distinct from an AMR indicator.

Surface energy, participation, $Q$, units, the zero-margin baseline, and logical
baseline deduplication were internally consistent in the inspected CSVs. A
thin-film surrogate can arithmetically produce participation above one, but
enormous values do not support a credible weak-perturbation $T_1$
interpretation. No numerical-convergence, causal-fix, or scientific-result
claim follows.

This reproduction locates the earliest confirmed defect in the Gmsh-generated
in-memory mesh, but it does not establish why meshing generated the degeneracy.
Pre-export and post-reload coordinate hashes and some floating summaries differ
with representation, so the evidence does not claim that all in-memory and
reloaded bytes or fields are equal. Crack displacement creating thin elements
is a separate hypothesis that requires full-precision pre-crack versus
post-crack element lineage. Causal linkage to the full solver and Surface-EPR
observations also remains unproven.

### Synthetic determinant illustration

For the deliberately synthetic points
$(0,0,0)$, $(1,0,0)$, $(0,1,0)$, and $(1,1,0)$, all four vertices lie in one
plane, so

$$
V = \frac{\left|\det\!\left[\mathbf{p}_1-\mathbf{p}_0,
\mathbf{p}_2-\mathbf{p}_0,\mathbf{p}_3-\mathbf{p}_0\right]\right|}{6}=0.
$$

This is an inert algebra example, distinct from the evidence-owner reproduction
above and not a reproduction of any private solver or Surface-EPR failure.

### Remaining investigation

A bounded finer-edge comparison was performed by the evidence owner, but it is
not established as a causal fix or an accepted Surface-EPR result.
Consumer-specific mesh controls, run outcomes, and inspection or relaunch
procedures remain outside this public archive. Full-precision pre-crack and
post-crack element lineage and complete solver and Surface-EPR causality remain
open. This documentation update ran no mesh or solver experiment, adds no
SCGSim validator, and prescribes no Gate, tuning, deletion, or fallback.
